content:
I printed what you sent. Here's how it came out:
wheel:
- 22.09 mm seat: goes in, pretty snug; holds upside down.
- the roof over the pocket: loose loops and tangles around the hole; hole partly closed.
spacer:
- I printed it, but I can't tell you how it came out.
bearing-coupon:
- 22.09 mm seat: goes in, pretty snug; holds upside down.

Send me the design again with submit_design, changed or unchanged, and I'll print it again from what you send.

reasoning:
I'm working out whether the top pocket has a roof at all, since it opens upward. The bottom pocket sits on the bed and needs no support, but the web above it is a 22 mm span, and I'm checking how that bridge holds up.

I'm weighing a few ways to avoid the 10 mm bore in the 22 mm web bridge, since bridging that span tends to sag and loop. Making the bore smaller doesn't solve it, so I'm looking at a conical or stepped roof, though the 3 mm web may be too thin for a 45° cone, so a ledge seat for the bearing race might work better.

I'm sizing a ledge seat for the outer race and checking whether a 45° cone from there down to the 5 mm bore would fit, but the cone needs about 4.5 mm of height and the bearing gap is only 3 mm, so that doesn't work. I'm considering printing the wheel with its axis horizontal, though a tread on its side would need supports, and then splitting it into two halves that print open-side-up, which avoids the bridge entirely but leaves the question of how to fasten the halves together.

I'm weighing whether two halves fastened with M3 screws into inserts would be simpler than keeping the single part. Another option is to model the bore closed with a thin skin layer so the 22 mm bridge has no hole to sag into, which would still need a bridge over the full pocket.

I'm checking whether the top pocket's roof can be left solid and then opened afterward, or whether it needs a membrane so the bridge doesn't sag. A thin 0.4 mm membrane in the bore would let the 22 mm bridge print cleanly, and the user could punch the hole out with a bolt or screwdriver once it's done.

I'm settling on a 0.4 mm membrane across the bottom of the bore, so the 22 mm bridge has a continuous skin to print on. The bore itself stays open above it, and the user can punch the membrane out afterward. I'm also checking that the pocket fit and the coupon's open-up pocket don't need any changes.

I'm settling the membrane's position: a 0.4 mm skin sits right above the pocket ceiling, with the bore opening above it, so the web is solid through that thin layer. I'm also planning to add a step in the manual for punching the membrane out, then update the criteria and resubmit with the same hardware list.

    pd = p.bearing_od + p.pocket_clear
    bot = cq.Workplane('XY').circle(pd/2).extrude(d)
    top = cq.Workplane('XY').workplane(offset=w-d).circle(pd/2).extrude(d)
    z0 = d + p.membrane_t
    bore = cq.Workplane('XY').workplane(offset=z0).circle(p.web_bore/2).extrude(w - z0)
    return wheel.cut(bot).cut(top).cut(bore)
"},{"id":"spacer","role":"final","material":"PLA","print_orientation":"Flat on the bed (axis vertical)","use_orientation":"Sits in the wheel's centre web between the two bearings' inner races, on the bolt","code":"def build(p):
    L = p.wheel_w - 2*p.pocket_depth
    return (cq.Workplane('XY').circle(p.spacer_od/2).circle((p.bolt_d+p.spacer_clear)/2).extrude(L))
"},{"id":"bearing-coupon","role":"coupon","material":"PLA","print_orientation":"Flat on the bed, pocket facing up","use_orientation":"Test print only, to check the bearing press fit","code":"def build(p):

    disc = cq.Workplane('XY').circle(p.coupon_od/2).extrude(p.coupon_t)
    pocket = cq.Workplane('XY').workplane(offset=p.coupon_t-p.coupon_depth).circle(pd/2).extrude(p.coupon_depth)
    bore = cq.Workplane('XY').circle(p.web_bore/2).extrude(p.coupon_t)
    return disc.cut(pocket).cut(bore)

It holds the two inner races apart, so the bolt clamps the inner races and the wheel spins on the outer races."}}], "manual": [{"n":"1","text":"Print the wheel and the spacer in black PLA, with the wheel's flat face down. That's intended.","parts":["wheel","spacer"]},{"n":"2","text":"Punch out the thin skin (0.4 mm) in the centre of the wheel. You should end up with a clean 10 mm hole through the web.","parts":["wheel"],"hardware":["bolt"]},{"n":"3","text":"Press one bearing into each face of the wheel until it stops against the centre web. Press on the outer ring only, using a flat board or a vise. Each bearing should stick out about 0.5 mm.","parts":["wheel"],"hardware":["bearing"]},{"n":"4","text":"Drop the spacer into the wheel's centre bore. It sits between the two bearings' inner rings.","parts":["spacer"]},{"n":"5","text":"Put an M8 washer on the bolt, then slide the bolt through the bearings and spacer. Put the second washer on the other side. The washers must touch only the bearings' inner rings, not the wheel body.","parts":["wheel","spacer"],"hardware":["bolt","washer","bearing"]},{"n":"6","text":"Fit the assembly into the door hanger bracket, pass the bolt through the bracket holes and tighten the lock nut. The wheel should spin freely with no rubbing on the bracket. Don't over-tighten the nut.","hardware":["bolt","locknut"]}], "questions": [{"text":"What is the length of your M8 bolt under the head? I assumed M8x50 as a placeholder. You need about 20 mm for the wheel stack, plus the bracket thickness, plus the nut."},{"text":"What is the rail profile (flat, rounded or V)? I couldn't get this measured, so the tread is flat with 1 mm chamfers."},{"text":"What is the gap between the bracket arms? I couldn't get this measured. The stack is about 17 mm of wheel and bearings plus 2 washers (about 20.2 mm total). If the gap is tighter, drop the washers or add spacers."},{"text":"How did the spacer come out? If it's hard to say, check that the M8 bolt slides through it and that it measures 3 mm long."}], "note": "Revision 2.
